graded_by: Claude (independent of the screen score), charts eyeballed
tape: The default CSP screen returned 14 names; 7 are bitcoin miners / AI datacenter that move as one (60-day return correlation 0.70 to 0.88).
IV rank sits under 25 on 13 of 14 names (52-week CBOE rank where available, otherwise our 3-month history). Premium is cheap on names that can gap 10%.
Every name cleared the screen's earnings filter; no report lands inside these expiries.
Last week's active-fund buying was memory: MU, SK Hynix, Samsung, SanDisk, WDC.
Gamma scan: 15 of 25 names in positive dealer gamma (pinning), 10 in negative (moves get amplified). Call walls overhead on 16.

setups.deskNote: Best of the miner cluster. The 11.5 strike is the 11.5K-OI put support line, price is back above the 21/55 EMAs and 14% over the 200. Firm quotes, 6.5K OI floor.
setups.whyNot: It is still a bitcoin trade. If BTC breaks, all seven miners go together, and 11.5 is only 1.2 ATRs away.
setups.fundOptionsNote: BLOX and ULTI (income ETFs) ran put spreads around 12-13 that expired Friday. Income overlays, not a view on direction.

setups.whyNot: Same bet as MARA (0.88 correlation). Sell one, not both. The 21 strike sits 20% above the 60-day low, so the real floor is well below you.
setups.fundOptionsNote: BLOX 22.5/23.5 put spread and ULTI legs expired Friday; income overlays.

setups.whyNot: Miner cluster (0.87 with MARA). IV rank 1: this is the cheapest the premium has been in a year, so you are paid the least exactly where the name can gap most.

setups.deskNote: 39.5 strike sits on the 39-41 put-OI shelf; deep, liquid chain.
setups.whyNot: Miner cluster. IV rank 0 and price is sitting right on its gamma flip (44): below it dealers amplify moves instead of dampening them.

Down 26% in 60 days, 18% under the 200, strike only 2.5% above the 60-day low, and just 766 OI at the strike. Thin exit on a falling chart.

setups.deskNote: Strongest trend on the list: higher lows since July, 36% over the 200.
setups.whyNot: Up 56% in 60 days and 10% over its 21 EMA. Selling puts after the run is how you get tagged on the snap back. Wait for a tag of the 21 EMA (~39) and sell the 36-37 put then.

setups.deskNote: Bounced off the August low (~36). The 41 strike sits under the 30K-OI put support near 40.
setups.whyNot: Wide quotes, +16% in five days, and IV rank near its 52-week low. Quantum cluster with RGTI (0.92). Only work it with a limit at mid.

setups.deskNote: The 15 strike is the 20K-OI support in a 15-18 range.
setups.whyNot: Moves in lockstep with IONQ (0.92), wide quotes, and it trades 71% below its high. If you want quantum, IONQ has the better chart.

setups.deskNote: Michael's own wheel name. The 7 strike is the 7K-OI support and just under the 7.23 gamma flip, which gets you in under $10 at a 6.58 basis.
setups.whyNot: Lower highs since May, 19% under the 200, 39 OI at the strike, and IV near a 3-month low. This is an adding-to-the-position decision, not a fresh setup. Limit orders only.

setups.deskNote: Richest IV on the list (rank 100) and 40 days out.
setups.whyNot: Just lost 22 support and sits near its 52-week low. IV rank 100 means something is being priced. Options volume 28 and OI floor 62: you may not get out.

setups.deskNote: $550 collateral makes it the small-account name.
setups.whyNot: Two contracts traded, wide quotes, 160 OI. The premium is theoretical until someone takes the other side.
Down 45% in 60 days, 36% under its 200 with ADX 31 (trending down, hard). A put here is a limit order to buy a falling knife. Plus 58 OI and wide quotes.

institutional.note: Memory was the buy: MU across 10 funds, plus Hynix, Samsung, SanDisk and WDC. Much of the jump in blended weight is Roundhill's DRAM, a 9-name memory fund at 27% MU, so read the fund count, not the weight. The file labels STX as Strike Energy; it is almost certainly Seagate. Selling was light and spread out (RCL the biggest).
